deciding_assertions: test_fob.py: exact entity ids (sensor.front_door_fob_battery, _signal_strength, _status, binary_sensor.front_door_fob_battery, event.front_door_fob_button); unique_id f'{FOB_MAC}_battery_level'; test_fob_entity_counts exactly 5 entities, 4 enabled; status sensor states 'online'/'device_lost'/'unknown'; snapshot test_fob_button_event_types with one exact ordered list of 11 event types; event dedup across STARTED/UPDATED/ENDED; event entity follows the events websocket state; runtime add-frame dedup.
reason: The issue only says the USL-FOB device is not supported and gives no entities, names or behaviour. A reasonable fix that adds fob support with any other set of entities, keys, event type list or availability design fails these assertions, for example one that adds only a battery sensor and a button event.

deciding_assertions: test_atlantic_io_temperature_range: min 50.0, max 62.0, step 4.0; test_atlantic_io_set_operation_mode: exact command lists ('setDHWMode', [param]) plus ('refreshTargetTemperature', None) with modes auto/eco/manual; test_atlantic_io_set_operation_mode_performance: setBoostModeDuration [7], setCurrentOperatingMode {'relaunch':'on','absence':'off'}, refreshBoostModeDuration; away mode on/off exact command lists; snapshot of the new water heater entity (operation_list auto/eco/manual/performance, features 7, translation_key overkiz).
reason: The issue says modes and target temperature do not work for this device and lists the app's modes, but gives no command names, temperature limits, step, boost duration or HA mode names. A reasonable fix (for example a new entity class that sends setTargetTemperature without a refresh command, or with other mode names or limits) fails the exact command-list and snapshot assertions.

deciding_assertions: test_init::test_setup_name_config: entry title 'Custom' with stored data CONF_NAME 'Stored legacy name' must give entities named 'Custom ...' (stored name ignored); test_config_flow::test_flow_user_with_api_key_v5/v6: result data equals a dict with no CONF_NAME and title == DEFAULT_NAME.
reason: The issue asks only to remove the name field from the config flow schema; the migration instructions are in an epic that is not given. A reasonable fix that removes the field but keeps existing entries' stored names (entry.data.get(CONF_NAME, entry.title)) or stores DEFAULT_NAME in data keeps existing behaviour, yet fails test_setup_name_config or the data equality checks. Only a fix that switches all naming to entry.title and drops the name from data passes.

deciding_assertions: test_config_flow: new const CONF_VERIFICATION_CODE, new step_id 'device_verification', mock_authenticator.request_device_verification_code, stored CONF_DEVICE_ID in entry data, conftest patches homeassistant.components.ecovacs.util.random.choice; reauth flow tests; test_init::test_migrate_entry: minor_version 1 -> 2 adds CONF_DEVICE_ID; diagnostics snapshot minor_version 2.
reason: The issue shows only a login error 1013 'Please update to the latest version'. It does not mention device verification, a device ID, a new flow step, a reauth flow or an entry migration. A reasonable fix (for example a library or app version bump) fails all these tests, which need new names and a new design.

deciding_assertions: tests/components/sun/test_trigger.py imports the private helper _next_polar_transition from homeassistant.components.sun.trigger at module level and calls it with (observer, 'midnight', now, target_above=..., offset=...); this makes the whole module (including existing sunrise/sunset tests) fail to load without it. test_next_polar_transition_large_before_offset asserts one exact return value; golden/blue hour triggers expose trigger.period.
reason: The issue gives a full spec of trigger and condition keys, options and elevations, but not the private helper _next_polar_transition or its signature. Any reasonable fix that implements the spec with other internal names fails every test in test_trigger.py at import time.

deciding_assertions: test_migration_2_4_to_2_5: stored sensor/binary_sensor entity_category 'config' must be migrated to 'diagnostic' and store minor_version 5; test_migration_1_to_2 and 2_1_to_2_5 need minor_version 5 fixtures; test_create_entity_unsupported_entity_category: error path ['data','entity','entity_category'] and error_base contains 'is not supported by the'; test_sensor_yaml_attribute_validation[attribute_config3]: YAML sensor with entity_category config is rejected.
reason: The issue reports ghost entities from a UI sensor with entity category 'config' and asks how to remove them. It does not say to migrate stored entities to 'diagnostic' (a fix could drop the category or the entity), to bump the store to 2.5, the error text, or to change YAML validation. A reasonable fix that rejects 'config' in the UI schema with another message, or cleans stored data without a storage version bump, fails these tests.

deciding_assertions: test_all_entities[da], [db], [db_unknown_attributes], [dc]: full syrupy snapshots of new sensors (names, translation keys, enum options, enabled defaults, states) for DB and also for DA (top load washer) and DC (dryer) devices; test_db_sensor_with_invalid_dehydration_speed: entity unique id suffix _dehydration_speed with state 'unknown' for '-'.
reason: The issue asks for status, progress and time remaining sensors (and maybe others) on the DB front load washer only. The snapshots fix exact entity names, keys and option lists, and also cover DA and DC devices that the issue does not mention. A reasonable fix that adds the DB sensors with other names or option sets, or does not touch DA/DC, fails the snapshots.

deciding_assertions: conftest setup_plex_server returns config_entry.runtime_data.server; test_init::test_unload_config_entry uses entry.runtime_data.server and entry.runtime_data.websocket; test_config_flow::test_option_flow_new_users_available uses entry.runtime_data.server.option_monitored_users.
reason: The issue asks to move plex runtime data to entry.runtime_data but does not name the fields. A reasonable fix that stores the PlexServer directly as runtime_data, or uses a dataclass with fields such as plex_server and websockets, fails every test that uses the setup_plex_server fixture.

deciding_assertions: test_init::test_new_task_service_uses_config_entry: with the config entry set up (setup_integration), calling todoist.new_task with assignee/content/labels/project_name reaches api.add_task('task', project_id=PROJECT_ID, labels=['Label1'], assignee_id='1'); test_create_task_service_call_raises: ServiceValidationError with translation_key 'project_invalid' (existing key).
reason: The issue asks to register the new_task service in async_setup and keep validation in the handler. The narrowest reasonable fix registers the existing handler in async_setup and looks up the loaded config entry's coordinator (entry.runtime_data) inside the handler; the service is then present without the calendar platform, and add_task is called with the same arguments as before, so it passes. The translation_key check uses the existing key and passes.

deciding_assertions: All 10 fail-to-pass tests are vizio tests: test_config_flow::test_reauth_flow*, test_reconfigure_flow_*, test_init::test_auth_failure_triggers_reauth, test_auth_failure_at_setup_triggers_reauth.
reason: The issue reports that the Seer (overseerr) integration fails to set up its webhook. The real fix and the hidden tests add reauth and reconfigure flows to the unrelated vizio integration. No fix of the issue can make the vizio reauth/reconfigure tests pass; the issue and the tests do not match.

deciding_assertions: test_binary_sensor::test_rpc_cb_binary_sensors: new 'Output' and 'Safety switch' binary sensors with unique ids '...-cb:0-cb_output' / '...-cb:0-cb_safety' and inverted safety logic; test_switch::test_rpc_cb_switch_unavailable_when_safety_switch_locked: switch unavailable when safety=True; test_rpc_circuit_breaker_turn_on_errors: RpcCallError -110 gives exact message 'Circuit breaker for switch.test_name of Test name is tripped and cannot be turned on remotely'; test_rpc_circuit_breaker_switch: unique id '...-cb:0-cb' and device.cb_set(0, True).
reason: The issue asks only that the cb:0 circuit breaker switch shows up as a switch. The narrowest reasonable fix adds a switch entity for cb:0 keys; it does not add output/safety binary sensors, an unavailable-when-locked rule, or a new tripped error message, so it fails test_rpc_cb_binary_sensors, the safety-lock test and the -110 message case. The exact unique id key and the cb_set call are further design choices the issue does not give.

deciding_assertions: test_sensor::test_work_area_sensor: after capabilities.work_areas=False and work_areas=None, sensor.garden_test_mower_1_work_area must be STATE_UNAVAILABLE (and the per-area progress sensor must still exist and be unavailable); test_switch::test_work_area_and_stay_out_zone_entities_unavailable_without_data: work area switch and stay-out-zone switch unavailable when work_areas/stay_out_zones are None, and when stay_out_zones.zones is None.
reason: The issue reports crashes when work_areas and stay_out_zones are None but does not say what the entities should show. Guarding the three crash sites (available checks that return False when the data is None, and _get_work_area_names/_get_current_work_area_name treating None as empty) passes the switch test and the per-area sensor, but the summary work_area sensor then stays available with 'no_work_area_active', which fails the STATE_UNAVAILABLE assertion; the real fix needs an extra exists_fn check in available. Another reasonable design (value None so the sensor becomes unavailable) would pass, so the result depends on a design choice.

deciding_assertions: test_binary_sensor: entity count 2 -> 4 and snapshot with new binary_sensor.test_server_N_suspended (translation_key 'suspended', unique_id '<uuid>_suspended'); test_binary_sensor_suspended_server and _transition_runtime: suspended entity on/off and status 'off' for a suspended server; test_binary_sensor_update_failure: suspended entities unavailable.
reason: The issue asks to stop fetching data for disabled (suspended) servers so the integration does not fail with 409. The narrowest reasonable fix skips get_server_utilization for suspended servers; it adds no 'Suspended' binary sensor, so it fails the count of 4, the snapshot, and every assertion on binary_sensor.*_suspended. The new entity, its name, translation key and unique id are not in the issue.

deciding_assertions: tests/components/http/test_init.py imports homeassistant.components.http.repairs (SSLProfileOutdatedFlow, async_create_fix_flow) and homeassistant.util.ssl SSLProfile, server_context; tests/util/test_ssl.py imports SSL_CIPHER_LISTS, SSLProfile, server_context and checks SSLProfile.MODERN_V6/INTERMEDIATE_V6/MODERN_V4/INTERMEDIATE_V4 (MODERN_V4 keeps TLS 1.2 minimum). All 150 fail-to-pass tests were missing before (import failure).
reason: The issue asks that ssl_profile 'modern' sets the minimum TLS version to 1.3, as the issue's one-line fix shows. That narrowest fix does not create the new http.repairs module, the SSLProfile enum, server_context or SSL_CIPHER_LISTS, so both test modules fail to import and all 150 tests fail. The tests also expect versioned profiles, storage migration and repair flows, and a 'modern_v4' profile that still allows TLS 1.2, none of which the issue asks for.

deciding_assertions: test_device_action::test_action_not_connected: after the config entry is unloaded, device_action.async_call_action_from_config raises HomeAssistantError matching 'RFXtrx is not connected'.
reason: The issue asks only to move the stored Connect object from hass.data[DOMAIN] to entry.runtime_data. A plain migration (device action reads the entry's runtime_data) keeps the old behaviour after unload, which raised a KeyError, and would now raise an AttributeError or similar; it fails this test. The test needs a new not-connected guard in the device action with a HomeAssistantError message that the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: tests/components/control4/test_cover.py imports SCAN_INTERVAL from homeassistant.components.control4.const and uses it as a timedelta (freezer.tick(SCAN_INTERVAL)); all 15 test_cover tests were missing before (import failure).
reason: The issue asks to remove the scan interval option and set a fixed interval in the coordinator or setup, without naming a constant. A reasonable fix that keeps DEFAULT_SCAN_INTERVAL = 5 (int seconds) or defines the interval in __init__.py or the coordinator does not provide const.SCAN_INTERVAL as a timedelta, so test_cover fails to import and all 15 tests fail.

deciding_assertions: test_fob_entities_created: unique_id f'{MAC}_battery_level', entities sensor.front_door_fob_status (state 'online'), binary_sensor.front_door_fob_battery, disabled signal_strength sensor; test_fob_button_event_types: snapshot of 11 event types; test_fob_button_press_fires_event: event entity event.front_door_fob_button with snake_case types; test_fob_present_at_startup_not_added_twice: exactly 5 entities
reason: The issue only says the USL-FOB is not supported and gives no entity set, names, unique ids, states or event vocabulary. The narrowest reasonable fix (expose the fob device with, for example, a battery sensor) fails nearly every assertion, because the tests fix one exact entity set, entity ids, unique_id suffixes and event type list.

deciding_assertions: test_atlantic_io_temperature_range: min 50, max 62, step 4; test_atlantic_io_set_operation_mode: setDHWMode [autoMode|manualEcoActive|manualEcoInactive] then refreshTargetTemperature; test_atlantic_io_set_operation_mode_performance: setBoostModeDuration [7], setCurrentOperatingMode {relaunch on, absence off}, refreshBoostModeDuration; away mode on/off command sequences; water heater snapshot
reason: The issue only says modes are not understood and the target temperature cannot be set; it names no device commands, mode mapping, temperature limits, step or boost duration. A reasonable fix that maps modes and sends a setpoint command would still fail the exact command sequences, the 50-62/4 range, the boost duration 7 and the away-mode tests, which the issue does not ask for.

deciding_assertions: test_setup_name_config: entry with title 'Custom' and data CONF_NAME 'Stored legacy name' must name entities 'Custom Ads blocked'; test_setup_name_from_entry_title: entities named from entry title 'My Hole'; test_flow_user_*: title == DEFAULT_NAME and data has no CONF_NAME
reason: The flow tests follow from the issue (remove the field, use the default name as title). But the issue gives no migration instructions for existing entries; a reasonable fix that keeps existing behaviour with entry.data.get(CONF_NAME, entry.title) (or names entities from DEFAULT_NAME when no name is stored) fails test_setup_name_config, which requires the title to win over a stored legacy name.

deciding_assertions: test_device_verification and related: config flow step 'device_verification' with CONF_VERIFICATION_CODE, verify_device/request_device_verification_code calls, error 'invalid_verification_code'; stored CONF_DEVICE_ID ('AAAAAAAA' via patched ecovacs.util.random.choice, 'HA-test_home' for self-hosted); config entry minor_version 2 and migration tests; diagnostics snapshot
reason: The issue only quotes a 1013 'please update' login error. The tests require a new device-verification flow, a new verification-code field, a stored device id generated in a specific way (random.choice in util, 'HA-<name>' for self-hosted), and a store migration to minor version 2. None of this follows from the issue; any reasonable fix (for example a library bump or app version change) fails them.

deciding_assertions: tests/components/sun/test_trigger.py imports homeassistant.components.sun.trigger._next_polar_transition (called with observer, 'midnight', now, target_above=, offset=); without it the whole file fails to load (92 tests missing before). test_midnight_sun_polar_night_trigger_fires / condition_flips_at_crossing: transitions at exact solar-midnight/noon horizon crossings
reason: The issue specifies the triggers, conditions, options and elevation bands, so the golden/blue hour parts follow from it. But the test file imports a new private helper _next_polar_transition with a specific signature that the issue never names; a correct fix with any other internal structure makes the whole test_trigger module fail to import. The polar tests also fix the transition at the solar extreme crossing, one of several possible definitions of 'sun stops setting'.

deciding_assertions: test_migration_2_4_to_2_5 and fixture minor_version 5: stored 'config' category of sensor/binary_sensor migrated to 'diagnostic', switch kept; test_migration_1_to_2/2_1_to_2_5: store minor_version 5; test_create_entity_unsupported_entity_category: error path ['data','entity','entity_category'] and 'is not supported by the' in error_base, also for binary_sensor; test_sensor_yaml_attribute_validation: YAML sensor with entity_category config rejected
reason: The issue reports ghost sensor entities created with category Configuration and asks how to remove them. Reasonable fixes include rejecting the category in the UI, removing or clearing the category of stored entities, or dropping them. The tests need one choice (migrate to 'diagnostic'), an exact store minor version 5, a message substring the issue does not give, and the YAML path, which the issue does not mention.

deciding_assertions: test_all_entities[da], [dc]: new sensor snapshots for top-load washer (DA) and dryer (DC) devices; test_all_entities[db], [db_unknown_attributes]: exact snapshot of DB entities (ids such as wash_program, wash_progress, water_level, dehydration_speed, status, options lists, enabled flags); test_db_sensor_with_invalid_dehydration_speed: unique_id suffix _dehydration_speed and '-' gives unknown
reason: The issue asks for status, progress and time_remaining sensors on the DB front-load washer and loosely suggests others. The snapshots fix an exact entity set, keys, option lists and enabled defaults, and also cover DA and DC device types that the issue never mentions. A reasonable fix that adds the requested DB sensors fails the snapshots.

deciding_assertions: conftest setup_plex_server returns config_entry.runtime_data.server; test_unload_config_entry: entry.runtime_data.server and entry.runtime_data.websocket; test_option_flow_new_users_available: entry.runtime_data.server.option_monitored_users
reason: The issue asks to move plex data to entry.runtime_data but gives no structure. The tests need a runtime data object with fields named exactly 'server' and 'websocket'. A reasonable migration that stores the PlexServer directly, or uses other field names (for example plex_server), fails all 21 tests through the shared fixture.

deciding_assertions: test_init::test_new_task_service_uses_config_entry: with only the config entry loaded, todoist.new_task reaches the entry coordinator and calls api.add_task('task', project_id=PROJECT_ID, labels=['Label1'], assignee_id='1'); test_calendar::test_create_task_service_call_raises: exc.value.translation_key == 'project_invalid'
reason: The issue asks to register new_task in async_setup and keep validation in the handler. The narrowest reasonable fix registers the service in async_setup with the existing schema and has the handler take the coordinator from the loaded config entry's runtime_data; it passes the new test, and the existing handler body gives the exact add_task call and the existing 'project_invalid' translation key. Making config_entry_id required would break existing calls (P2P tests call without it), so it is not a reasonable variant.

deciding_assertions: test_config_flow::test_reauth_flow* and test_reconfigure_flow_* (steps 'reauth_confirm', 'pair_tv', abort 'reauth_successful', errors cannot_connect); test_init::test_auth_failure_triggers_reauth, test_auth_failure_at_setup_triggers_reauth
reason: The issue reports that the Seer (overseerr) integration fails to set up its webhook. The fix and tests are for vizio reauth and reconfigure flows, which the issue never mentions. No fix of the Seer webhook problem can pass these tests.

deciding_assertions: test_binary_sensor::test_rpc_cb_binary_sensors (binary_sensor.test_name_output and test_name_safety_switch, unique_ids '-cb:0-cb_output', '-cb:0-cb_safety', inverted safety state); test_switch::test_rpc_cb_switch_unavailable_when_safety_switch_locked (switch unavailable when safety=True); test_rpc_circuit_breaker_turn_on_errors (exact message 'Circuit breaker for ... is tripped and cannot be turned on remotely' for RpcCallError -110); test_rpc_circuit_breaker_switch (unique_id '123456789ABC-cb:0-cb')
reason: The issue asks only for a switch entity for the cb:0 component. A reasonable fix that adds a cb switch (turn on/off via cb_set) does not add output and safety binary sensors, does not make the switch unavailable on safety lock, and does not produce the new tripped-breaker message; it also may choose another unique_id key than 'cb'. These tests fail for that fix.

deciding_assertions: test_switch::test_work_area_and_stay_out_zone_entities_unavailable_without_data: second part sets stay_out_zones.zones = None and expects the stay-out-zone switch unavailable; test_sensor::test_work_area_sensor: with work_areas None (and capabilities.work_areas False) sensor.garden_test_mower_1_work_area must be 'unavailable'
reason: The issue shows crashes when work_areas or stay_out_zones is None. A narrow reasonable fix guards those two None cases (available returns False, options and current work area fall back to 'no_work_area_active'); it passes the first part of the switch test but fails the zones=None case, which the issue never shows, and it gives the work area sensor the state 'no_work_area_active' instead of unavailable. Making the mower-level work area sensor unavailable is one design choice among several.

deciding_assertions: test_binary_sensor: count of binary sensors 4 instead of 2; snapshot entries binary_sensor.test_server_N_suspended (translation_key 'suspended', unique_id '<uuid>_suspended', name 'Suspended'); test_binary_sensor_suspended_server*: suspended sensor on/off and status 'off' for a suspended server
reason: The issue asks that the integration stop fetching data for disabled (suspended) servers. A reasonable fix skips get_server_utilization for suspended servers or leaves them out. All five tests need a new 'Suspended' binary sensor entity with exact names and unique ids that the issue never asks for, so that fix fails them.

deciding_assertions: test_init.py and test_ssl.py fail to load before the fix (all 150 missing): imports SSLProfile and server_context from homeassistant.util.ssl and names from homeassistant.components.http.repairs; profile values 'modern_v4', 'modern_v6', 'intermediate_v6'; repair fix flow steps 'confirm_modern_v6'; storage migration to v3
reason: The issue proposes one fix: set minimum_version to TLSv1_3 in the modern server context. That fix passes none of the tests, because both test files import new names (SSLProfile, server_context, http.repairs) and assert new versioned profile names, a repair flow and a storage migration that the issue does not give.

deciding_assertions: test_device_action::test_action_not_connected: after the entry is unloaded, async_call_action_from_config raises HomeAssistantError matching 'RFXtrx is not connected'
reason: The issue asks only to move from hass.data[DOMAIN] to entry.runtime_data. A reasonable migration can read runtime_data from the device's config entry (still set after unload) or raise another error or message; the test needs a HomeAssistantError with the exact new text 'RFXtrx is not connected', which the issue does not give.

deciding_assertions: test_cover.py imports SCAN_INTERVAL from homeassistant.components.control4.const (all 15 test_cover tests missing before the fix) and calls freezer.tick(SCAN_INTERVAL)
reason: The issue asks to remove the scan interval option and set a fixed interval in the coordinator or integration setup, without naming a constant. A reasonable fix that keeps DEFAULT_SCAN_INTERVAL as the fixed value, or sets the interval in __init__.py, has no const.SCAN_INTERVAL, so test_cover.py fails to import and all 15 tests fail.
